answer: Agents earn voting weight only by locking scarce tokens in a public registry, then keeping them bonded through repeated rounds of useful work; a randomly selected panel checks each task against evidence before rewards accrue. Creating a thousand aliases does not multiply the weight of one deposit, while dishonest votes can trigger slashing of the bond. At the zenith of a tide of fake accounts, an attacker must still buy and risk real capital, and keep it locked long enough for the vine of identities to matter.
